question: ADOPTION item 37 phase 2: can nanoRSI run complete, real agent tasks (ALFWorld games, engine-scored) end to end, and does gated skill evolution improve a strong base agent on them?

task_source.benchmark: ALFWorld (alfworld/alfworld, MIT; TextWorld engine, MIT; ALFRED data)
task_source.games: local alfworld-download json_2.1.1 cache; deterministic selection 4 train / 6 validation (train split) + 6 seen (valid_seen) + 6 unseen (valid_unseen); games not redistributed
task_source.adaptations: authored game runner (re-exec under a Python 3.12 + alfworld interpreter), evaluator overlay grading the engine won flag, initial operating skill; stock proposer/adapters/model bridge untouched

settings.rebuild_reasons: (1) runner missing propose mode - three attempts burned; (2) alfworld skill not registered in [agent] skills and thinking not disabled - bridge returned empty content and the proposer saw an empty surface; both bugs were fixed in the generator and are covered by tests

baseline_validation.note: two baseline runs of the same six validation games differ by one game (0.667 vs 0.833) - the observed panel noise band is +/-1 game (0.167), larger than plausible single-edit skill effects at this agent strength

search_outcomes.proposal: placement single-command rule and stop-after-placement guidance (attempt1-proposal.diff)

final_panel_test_12_games.split: 6 seen layouts + 6 unseen layouts; every condition solved 12/12
final_panel_test_12_games.interpretation: ceiling effect: glm-5.3 solves this frozen test subset with or without the initial skill, so skill evolution has no measurable headroom here; the null is about this regime, not about guidance editing in general

train_panels: attempt train panels 4/4, 4/4, 3/4 - the proposer received feedback from at most 4 games per attempt (thin signal by design of this small pack)

usage.episodes_total_workspace3: baseline 10 games + 3 attempts x 10 games + final 36 game-conditions

audit: zero expected-answer leakage, zero silent bypass, panel ok; verify lineage ok. Game tasks have no expected_files content, so the leakage screen is structural here: answers exist only as winning action sequences inside the engine
honest_negative: No accepted improvement in this study. The gate correctly blocked one harmful edit and two ties. Combined with the 12/12 ceiling on all final conditions, the small-pack + strong-agent regime cannot demonstrate skill-evolution gains; the platform capability (real agent tasks, engine-scored, frozen contract) is what this study establishes.
limits: One seed, one repeat, three attempts, 4 train / 6 validation / 12 test games, one strong model tier. Panel noise (+/-1 game) exceeds single-edit effects; splits are small by cost necessity; author-reported ALFWorld numbers (ReAct/Reflexion/ExpeL etc.) use different models, splits and budgets and are not reproduced. Follow-ups queued: larger train split and more attempts, flash-tier agent for headroom, noise-band-aware gating (ADOPTION 38 protocol), harder task-type mix.
